CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for anxiety management and breast lumps.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents for office follow-up. She was recently started on buspar by Dr. Brown for anxiety treatment. She reports significant anxiety in November and December that she described as "brutal." The anxiety typically began during work hours and often preceded her period—she noted that the week before her menstrual cycle, her anxiety would escalate significantly, which actually helped her predict when her period was coming. Subsequently, her anxiety began occurring at random times without clear triggers.

Patient was on progesterone during this time (initiated by Dr. Ward for period regulation). Dr. Ward also started her on Singulair, noting that this medication can potentially cause anxiety. Patient attributes her anxiety episodes in part to significant work-related stress. She works in a healthcare setting and led the process of delivering COVID test results to patients during the pandemic. Her facility also went through a "golive" in November and December, which was stressful. Additionally, she helped establish evaluation centers and a COVID clinic, which she found demanding. She expressed feeling guilty about her anxiety given that she was not on the front lines in the ICU like the physicians and nurses she worked with.

Patient recently discontinued Camila birth control because she experienced an unusually high level of hunger and was eating constantly; since discontinuing this medication, her appetite has normalized and she feels better. She reports weight loss over the past 6 months.

Currently, her anxiety is well-controlled on buspar. Regarding breast symptoms: Patient has persistent breast lumps, which feel smaller than previously noted but are still present. She reports tenderness in the left breast, particularly inferiorly, which she notes was also present during her previous breastfeeding with clogged ducts. She is concerned about these lumps given her age (46 years) and her family history (mother diagnosed with breast cancer at approximately age 45).

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Anxiety: currently controlled on buspar
Weight: weight loss over past 6 months
Breasts: persistent lumps, smaller than previously; left breast tenderness
Genital: itching/discomfort responsive to weekly topical cream; refill needed
Other systems: not specifically discussed

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Breast lumps/cysts
Abnormal pap smear approximately 2009 (required surveillance every six months, subsequently normalized)
Breastfeeding with clogged ducts and other complications

MEDICATIONS
Buspar (for anxiety)
Progesterone (for period regulation)
Singulair (indication not specified in visit)
Topical cream for genital discomfort (used once weekly; name not specified; patient needs refill)
Previous: Camila birth control (discontinued due to increased appetite)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother: diagnosed with breast cancer at approximately age 45

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in healthcare setting. During the COVID pandemic, she led the process of delivering COVID test results to patients and helped establish evaluation centers and COVID clinics, which she found stressful. Married; husband has not received COVID vaccine and daughter shares his concerns about vaccine safety. Son has received first dose of COVID vaccine. Patient has received COVID vaccine.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally on deep inspiration
Neck: Palpable small lumps/nodules noted
Breasts: Bilateral lumps present, smaller than previously noted but still palpable. Right breast slightly denser on palpation. Left breast with tenderness on palpation, particularly inferiorly.
Pelvic exam: Normal appearance

RESULTS
Pap smear from 2019: Negative/negative

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety disorder: Currently well-controlled on buspar. Likely multifactorial etiology including work-related stress related to COVID response and pandemic responsibilities, possible hormonal influence from progesterone, and normal aging process. Patient to continue current buspar therapy.

2. Breast lumps/masses: Patient has persistent palpable bilateral breast lumps that have not changed in size on examination. Discussed benign etiologies including cysts and fibroadenomas. Given patient's age (46 years), family history of breast cancer, and her significant concern about the lumps, breast specialist referral offered and accepted. Specialist will likely perform in-office ultrasound as part of their physical examination and will have greater experience with decision-making regarding possible procedures. Referral to be sent; specialist will contact patient within the next couple of business days to schedule appointment.

3. Cervical cancer screening: Last Pap smear in 2019 was normal (negative/negative). History of abnormal Pap smear approximately 2009 (subsequently resolved with surveillance). Plan to repeat Pap smear for surveillance given prior abnormality and current stress/potential for immune system effects.

4. Genital discomfort: Patient reports itching/discomfort managed well with weekly topical cream application. Patient to obtain refill.
